note: Twenty request phrasings with hand-annotated predicate vectors. CI tests the vector -> outcome half deterministically. The phrasing -> vector half needs a model and is a script, not a test. These annotations and the rule table share an author: CI checks self-consistency between two artefacts from one hand, not correctness against an external standard.

cases.phrasing: draw our microservice call graph as a subway map
cases.why: A substrate constrains how it is drawn, not what it is. The graph survives; stacked blocks are refused.

cases.phrasing: show the org chart for the platform team
cases.why: A tree is also a graph, so both fire; the evidence overlaps, so this is one figure and not a composition.

cases.phrasing: cross-section of a lithium cell with each layer labelled
cases.why: A scene refuses the graph preset outright, however well boxes and arrows would render.

cases.phrasing: deployment topology with callouts explaining the failover path
cases.why: Two candidates clear the floor on disjoint evidence — it is genuinely two things.

cases.phrasing: p99 latency over the last thirty days
cases.why: A series with a scale, asked for as a chart: the chart preset now serves this directly rather than refusing it.

cases.phrasing: the four stages of our onboarding, one after another
cases.why: Ordered stages with transitions are a graph; plain flow adds nothing that outranks it.

cases.phrasing: list the six services we run, no relationships needed
cases.why: An unordered set with no relations is the plain case, and the plain case must stay reachable.

cases.phrasing: mind map of everything we know about the incident
cases.why: Single-rooted hierarchy; the mindmap outranks the general graph.

cases.phrasing: floor plan of the office with the fire exits marked
cases.why: Scene plus annotation; the substrate refuses blocks and the scene refuses the graph.

cases.phrasing: how the request flows from the load balancer to the database
cases.why: The honest flowchart case. Defaulting to a graph is only wrong when the content is not one.

cases.phrasing: anatomy of the engine block with the parts called out
cases.why: The figure class no competitor serves, and the reason the repertoire exists.

cases.phrasing: our dependency tree, showing what pulls in what
cases.why: Asserting BOTH hierarchy and graph means it is not a strict tree — dependency graphs have diamonds. The general graph is correct; this fixture originally expected mindmap and the rule table was right to disagree.

cases.phrasing: the state machine for an order, including the cancelled path
cases.why: States and transitions are a graph in the plainest sense.

cases.phrasing: a labelled diagram of the water cycle over a landscape
cases.why: A substrate under a scene; the graph is refused even though evaporation and rainfall are arrows.

cases.phrasing: compare the three storage tiers side by side
cases.why: A comparison with no relations between the items is still a set.

cases.phrasing: market share by vendor as a pie chart
cases.why: The chart preset shipped bars only: a wedge is not a box, so 'pie' is not in the idiom vocabulary and nothing favours any preset. This is now the out-of-repertoire case 'none' is reachable from, in the chart preset's own honest boundary rather than the whole idiom being unserved.

cases.phrasing: the network topology drawn over a map of the campus
cases.why: Second substrate case; confirms the idiom constrains rather than restructures.

cases.phrasing: show the memory layout of this struct, field by field, with byte offsets
cases.why: Deliberately outside the vocabulary's centre. A packed linear extent has no structure value, so it surfaces as an unknown predicate instead of being forced into the nearest wrong bucket.

cases.phrasing: an annotated schematic of the signal path through the amplifier
cases.why: Scene disqualifies the graph outright even though the content is also a graph; disqualification beats weight.

cases.phrasing: just show me the three inputs and the one output
cases.why: The smallest possible request must not escalate into a graph.
